_comment: Exercise registry. Outline exercises are rendered by exercise.html?id=<id>; adding one of Khan's outlines is a JSON entry here, NOT a new page — but the outline text MUST be transcribed verbatim from a published Khan volume, never paraphrased from memory. Two volumes are transcribed so far: 'An Exercise in Understanding the Qur'an' (2013, surahs 85-114; sourceIds=khan-exercise-2013) and 'An Introduction to Understanding the Qur'an with Examples' (2011, six worked surahs; sourceIds=khan-introduction-2011, page number in provenanceHtml). heading/note values are trusted site-authored HTML. The root-spotting entry configures exercise-roots.html; its surah list is safe to extend to any surah since the recurring-root answer key is computed live from data/morphology/.

exercises.title: Coherence reading: Surah al-Asr (103)
exercises.tileDesc: Propose the structure of Surah 103 verse by verse, then compare your reading against the outline in Irfan Ahmad Khan's An Exercise in Understanding the Qur'an (2013).
exercises.provenanceHtml: outline structure from Irfan Ahmad Khan, An Exercise in Understanding the Qur'an: An Outline Study of the Last Thirty Divine Discourses (Surah 85 to Surah 114), Association of Quranic Understanding, 2013. ISBN 9781567447736. Khan's outline for Surah al-Asr is one of thirty surah outlines in the volume; Sources for the full citation.

outline.heading: Verse 1. Oath.
outline.note: Setting the cosmological frame by which the discourse will be measured.

outline.heading: Verse 2. Negative claim.
outline.note: The universal condition of loss.

outline.heading: Verse 3. Exception with conditions.
outline.note: Four conjoined qualifications that constitute the exception: faith, righteous deeds, mutual exhortation to truth, mutual exhortation to patience.

exercises.tileDesc: Propose the structure of Surah 96 verse by verse, then compare your reading against the outline in Irfan Ahmad Khan's An Introduction to Understanding the Qur'an with Examples (2011).
exercises.provenanceHtml: outline structure from Irfan Ahmad Khan, An Introduction to Understanding the Qur'an with Examples (compiled by Tanveer Azmat), Association for Qur'anic Understanding, 2011, p. 38. Distributed by the AQU at quranicunderstanding.com; Sources for the full citation.

outline.heading: [Āyāt 1–5] “Read in the name of your Lord
outline.note: Who created Man from a clot.” God, The Most Generous, taught Man to read and write. The Divine Book will teach Man What Man couldn't have learned by himself?

outline.heading: [Āyāt 6–8] The human situation
outline.note: Transgression in the human world: No sense of accountability. Those who are well-off act arrogantly. Tell them: “To your Lord is the Return”.

outline.heading: [Āyāt 9–14] Reading of the Book creates a reaction — The Divine review on the reaction
outline.note: 'Just see: how immoral and irrational it is! (This transgressor) would not even let a servant pray!! Did he not even consider: maybe the reader is on the right path, calling people to piety? If it was the case, and even then, this opponent turns away and gives him a lie, does he not know that God is watching?'

outline.heading: [Āyāt 15–18] Warning to the transgressor, to embolden the Reader
outline.note: If he does not stop, God will take an action and then none will be able to help him.

outline.heading: [Ayah 19] The concluding remark
outline.note: No compromise in delivering the Tawhidic message. The reading aims at bringing the servant nearer to his Lord: 'Prostrate and get nearness to God'.

exercises.provenanceHtml: outline structure from Irfan Ahmad Khan, An Introduction to Understanding the Qur'an with Examples (compiled by Tanveer Azmat), Association for Qur'anic Understanding, 2011, p. 45. Distributed by the AQU at quranicunderstanding.com; Sources for the full citation.

outline.heading: [Ayah 1] introduces the subject: Who are the opponents?
outline.note: If you know who the people are, that stands in the way of the Qur'anic Movement, then you can understand why they are doing so.

outline.heading: [Ayah 2 & āyah 3] together provide the answer:
outline.note: These are the same people who are unconcerned with the plight of the alienated or marginalized sections of human society. They would not care for the establishment of a system that would eliminate poverty and hunger. [They may look like very religious people. They became enemies of the Religion because it emphasizes their duty to the deprived and marginalized people.]

outline.heading: [Āyāt 4–6] remove the misunderstanding of the simple-minded who wonder why some traditionally religious people are standing in the way of the Religion.
outline.note: [These central āyāt underline: False religiosity is doomed. Worship is not a cultural function. If hearts are devoid of the presence of God, the traditional prayer is of no value, however impressive it may look from the outside!]

outline.heading: [Ayah 7] concludes:
outline.note: What good is their religion if they would not help the needy even with a small act of kindness!

outline.heading: [Ayah 1] Proclamation from the Divine Authority:
outline.note: “We have granted you (O Prophet!) the Kauthar, i.e. something whose blessings will go on increasing!” [The understanding of the Quran will grow with the progress in human knowledge. As humanity will strive to follow its guidance, the whole world will be filled with blessings: peace, justice and happiness.]

outline.heading: [Ayah 2] The central āyah explains what the Recipient should, therefore, do:
outline.note: i) make salah (a statement full of meaning!), ii) make sacrifice (a statement full of meaning!).

outline.heading: [Ayah 3] The concluding āyah tells the Recipient of the Kauthar not to worry
outline.note: about the opposition of the Qur'anic Movement: As the movement shall proceed further, gradually all the opposition will wither away.

outline.heading: [Ayah 1] The very first āyah introduces the subject:
outline.note: What to say to those who rejected our message and who are putting pressure upon us to leave our Tawhidic mission altogether or make some adjustment in our stand. [In fact, they have already rejected our message; but they are eager to talk to us in order to make a bargain!]

outline.heading: [Āyāt 2–5] Tell them: no good shall come out of our trying to convert each other:
outline.note: Ayah 2 and āyah 3 state: we have fundamental religious differences. '(When I, i.e., the Prophet, received the Divine Guidance that God and God alone is to be worshiped), as your well-wisher, I invited you to it, but now it is quite clear that you are not going to change your religious position'. Ayah 4 and āyah 5 repeat, it is quite clear that each of the two parties is quite firm in its stand. No one is going to change, however, hard you try that I change my religion or I try that you change your religion.

outline.heading: [Ayah 6] Peaceful co-existence is possible:
outline.note: The present conflict can be resolved, if we agree that every individual is free to choose his/her religion and that we should not put any kind of pressure on anyone to change one's religion.

outline.heading: [Ayah 1] The introductory āyah states in clear terms that God is just one.
outline.note: Any effort to bring plurality or duality in the Being of God is not permitted at all.

outline.heading: [Ayah 2] states the essential point explaining the nature of the Being of God:
outline.note: God is the Samad — the Being upon Whom all beings depend and Who does not depend upon anyone else.

outline.heading: [Ayah 3] clarifies that it is confusing to use, in connection with God, a language that we use to designate human relations.
outline.note: God is not father or mother of someone; nor is God, son or daughter of someone.

outline.heading: [Ayah 4] Concludes:
outline.note: No being is like (matching) God!
